resolution.note:
Both refuters killed every blocking finding, so the row stamps PASS:verify-refuted and this REVISE stays as the record. writing §13 (value-prop / positioning framing belongs in sales copy, not student-facing body) line 10: scope: The finding does not hold on four counts.

(a) Rule text. I read check_writing §13 at its current wording with `curriculum/evals/scripts/rule.js writing 13`. It bans positioning framing that defends against critiques such as vendor-story, marketing-deck, consultancy-pap or aspirational-frame, and it lists flag phrases. The sentence matches none of those phrases. The hard sub-rule targets the literal word "vendor" ("treat *vendor* in student-facing body as suspect"). The line contains no "vendor". The judge's "banned word vendor in other words" extends the rule beyond its text. The sentence also does not defend the curriculum against a critique or reassure the student. It states what the less-access stance costs sellers.

(b) Dated, pre-authorising notes. The home lecture's maintainer block (`curriculum/lectures/practice-of-risk.md`, "2026-09-23, iteration 2") records this exact sentence. It says: "one sentence under *The best mitigation is the door you don't open* names what the less-access stance costs the seller, this training included; the stance rubric's against-interest rung at M4... Register check: a claim about the buyer's decision, `check_writing §13`." So §13 was considered for this sentence and accepted. The lecture's Quality line shows writing PASS afterwards.

(c) Deliberate restoration. Commit fb6b411e (2026-11-13) restored the line after compaction cut it. Its message is "restore the two against-our-own-interest lines compaction cut (M4 door you don't open...)", with the Big Idea unchanged at n=12. The story-depth judges cite it repeatedly as the strongest stance line: quartet-a101-iter2 judges 1 and 3, a101-full-r1 and r2 judge-3, and apt101-handbook-r1 judge-1. `curriculum/story-craft.md` makes stance a required craft element. The proposed fix ("Expect a closed door to cost you a feature. It is still the right call.") would remove the stance the maintainer restored. Cutting is a body change to a student-facing slide.

(d) The sentence-structure complaint is not a §13 matter. It has one colon, and the register-flag and sentence passes in `curriculum/language/` kept the sentence (the 2026-11-13 sentence-index added it).

One factual gap: `curriculum/slides/door-you-dont-open.md` has no maintainer block of its own, so the accept note lives only in the home lecture. That is how slide files are borrowed and judged at home per `curriculum/CLAUDE.md`, so it does not weaken the refutation.

The 7-module versus 8-module question does not affect this slide. / harm: The finding fails on harm, on fit with §13, and on the cost of the fix.

**What §13 covers.** §13 (check_writing.md line 93) targets body prose that defends against vendor-story, marketing-deck or consultancy critiques. Its flag phrases are "not an aspirational X", "not a vendor Y", "this isn't marketing" and similar. Its hard sub-rule is about the literal word *vendor*. Line 10 contains none of these phrases and not the word "vendor". The judge's "banned word vendor in other words" is a paraphrase test the rule does not state. The sentence is also the reverse of defensive positioning: it tells the student the training's own seller loses something. That is a claim about the cost of a scoping decision, not a pitch.
